knownCaveats.title: 15 CONTENT_DIFFERENCE/BLOCKING shadow comparisons against production's real corpus
knownCaveats.detail: With the release active on a production-shaped corpus, the resolver is healthy on all 35 citations (RESOLVER_FAILURE 35 -> 0) and 27 resolve APPROVED_EXACT -- but 15 of those 27 classify CONTENT_DIFFERENCE and therefore BLOCKING, because production carries the full eCFR section dump (56,026 bytes for 1910.1200) where the governed record carries the reviewed 1,141-byte clause-accurate artifact. This is NOT a release defect: every BLOCKING record resolved with resolverHealth OK and governedBackingState APPROVED_EXACT, every digest reproduces, and the corpus is byte-identical. KG-5A's 'release active' column showed EXACT_MATCH on all 35 only because it ran on a corpus that had been REPLACED by the governed rows -- the step KG-5A then proved unsafe. Cross-checked two independent ways: KG-5A's reconciliation found 18 PRODUCTION_ROW_CONTENT_DIFFERS, of which 3 are NEW_REVIEW_REQUIRED and never reach a content comparison; 18 - 3 = 15. BLOCKING means 'would put a materially wrong claim in front of a customer IF GOVERNED MODE WERE ENABLED' -- it does not block SHADOW, which is customer-invisible, and it does not block activation with the cutover variables absent.
knownCaveats.whyNotYetAuthoritative: The KG-5B SHADOW comparison selected its legacy input with the repository's prefix-insensitive matcher (normalizeCitationForMatch), NOT by exercising the live hydrateStandardReferences customer path. 15 is therefore a corroborated DISCOVERY count, not an authoritative customer-path equivalence result. The difference may represent a true regulatory content difference, a storage/citation granularity difference, the governed artifact being an exact subsection of a larger legacy section dump, a normalization-only difference, a resolver pairing difference, or another evidence-backed classification. It must not be prejudged.
knownCaveats.resolution: KG-5C re-measured all 15 through the REAL customer path on both body-text tiers. The KG-5B PAIRING was correct and the count of 15 is confirmed -- what was too coarse was the classification. All 15 classify GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING on Path A and Path B: the delivered text is byte-for-byte the frozen reviewed artifact, the record is approved against its exact checksum, and a clause-by-clause review is recorded. Delivery fidelity is 27/27 DELIVERS_REVIEWED_ARTIFACT with zero approved badges on non-reviewed content. Not blocking.

rootCauseGovernance.statement: A failing test, comparator, harness, customer-path observation or production SHADOW discrepancy demonstrates a SYMPTOM. It does NOT by itself identify the component that must be modified.
requiredSequence: identify the authoritative layer that owns that contract
determine whether the implementation, source data, review state, resolver, presentation layer or instrumentation violates it
modify ONLY the owning layer unless evidence proves a cross-layer change is required
verify the correction at the boundary where the contract is observable
rootCauseGovernance.forbiddenLoop: observation -> edit -> rerun -> different observation -> edit again
prohibitions: Do not modify correct upstream or customer-facing behaviour to satisfy incorrect downstream instrumentation. If executable evidence proves the implementation satisfies the documented contract but a test or comparator disagrees, repair the test or comparator and classify the finding INSTRUMENTATION.
Do not reopen a protected architectural conclusion without new contradictory evidence.
Do not make multiple speculative edits across layers to make a metric turn green.
Do not weaken an invariant, threshold, predicate or production control to make a discrepancy disappear.
Do not create another KG implementation phase because a non-blocking defect was discovered.
rootCauseGovernance.instrumentationRepairProof: The proof that a repair was not made to move a number is that the verdict does not move. State the measured verdict before and after. An instrumentation repair that moves the verdict needs its own root-cause analysis.
rootCauseGovernance.ifRootCauseCannotBeEstablished: Classify UNCLASSIFIED, capture the evidence, and stop progression toward CUTOVER until resolved. Do not edit implementation to make an unexplained observation go away.

find the contract in the layer tables -> that is the owner
if it appears in two layers, the owner is the one closest to the contract's definition, not where the symptom surfaced
if it appears in none, the contract is undocumented: establish and document it before editing
record the owner in the open-issues register before remediation

H3_unreviewedFallback.hypothesis: For every unreviewed record, governed delivery is withheld and legacy behaviour is preserved exactly.
H3_unreviewedFallback.refutedBy: any governed content constructed for a record with no effective approval

H4_resolverPathBehaviour.hypothesis: Both paths resolve through the single seam and therefore cannot disagree - this is STRUCTURAL (they share resolveStandard()), and SHADOW telemetry does NOT independently re-establish it: the v2 event carries no resolver-path identifier (KG5D-DISC-01). What SHADOW can evaluate is that every observation's resolution is internally consistent with its own pinned release, and that the Path A / Path B representation difference accounts for every content-length difference observed.
H4_resolverPathBehaviour.refutedBy: an observation whose backing, citation or release is inconsistent with its own pinned release

H5_badgeAndProvenanceTruthfulness.hypothesis: customerVisible is false throughout, projectGovernedDisplay() contributes {}, and no governed provenance is written; knowledgeReleaseId is NULL on every row.
H5_badgeAndProvenanceTruthfulness.refutedBy: any governed key in a payload, or any non-NULL provenance

H6_absenceOfCustomerMutation.hypothesis: The customer receives the pristine legacy run on every request; the stable field set is identical to LEGACY; customerOutputUnchanged is true on every event.
H6_absenceOfCustomerMutation.refutedBy: any difference in a field derived as stable, or an INDETERMINATE invariance check

H7_instrumentationFidelity.hypothesis: Telemetry distinguishes legacy from governed representations, attributes every observation to its correlation, finding and pinned release, and every event passes the v2 privacy guard. Resolver-path attribution is OUT OF SCOPE - the field does not exist.
H7_instrumentationFidelity.refutedBy: a comparison that cannot name its release, or a field outside the v2 allowlist

H8_releaseIdentity.hypothesis: Every observation names the single explicitly intended release and its manifest checksum, captured in the same query as the active-pointer read.
H8_releaseIdentity.refutedBy: any observation naming a different release, or a manifest/pointer mismatch

productionShadowProtocol.hypothesisEvaluationRule: A hypothesis is evaluated, not assumed. A hypothesis with zero qualifying observations is UNPROVEN, never 'passed'. The KG-4D per-observation non-vacuity floor (D-54) applies: three slices have been fooled by an equality oracle comparing two broken observations.
productionShadowProtocol.everyObservationMustMapToAHypothesis: Every SHADOW observation must map to a predefined hypothesis or be explicitly classified as an unexpected observation. Vague goals such as 'see what happens in production' are not permitted.

EXPECTED_EQUIVALENCE.definition: Governed and legacy outcomes are materially equivalent under the applicable contract.

EXPECTED_GOVERNED_REVIEWED_RENDERING.definition: The governed representation differs from legacy but exactly matches the reviewed governed artifact. This is NOT a defect merely because the bytes differ.
entryRequirements: reviewer-approved in the active release against the exact checksum
a clause-by-clause review recorded in a named KG phase artifact
the delivered text byte-identical to the frozen payload.canonicalText

RESOLUTION_DIFFERENCE.definition: Legacy and governed paths select materially different citation identities or applicability outcomes.

CONTENT_DIFFERENCE.definition: For a record expected to satisfy the same content contract, the delivered governed artifact differs unexpectedly.

MISSING_GOVERNED_RECORD.definition: A request expected to resolve through an approved governed record cannot do so.
MISSING_GOVERNED_RECORD.defaultDisposition: investigate; may be DEFECT_NONBLOCKING corpus backlog

REVIEW_STATE_VIOLATION.definition: Unreviewed content is treated as approved/governed customer content, or approval state is otherwise misrepresented.

CUSTOMER_MUTATION.definition: SHADOW changes the authoritative customer response or customer-visible behaviour.

INSTRUMENTATION_ERROR.definition: The comparator, telemetry or harness is observing the wrong field, representation, citation identity or lifecycle state - measuring the wrong contract.
INSTRUMENTATION_ERROR.defaultDisposition: INSTRUMENTATION; repair the measurement, not production

UNCLASSIFIED.definition: The evidence does not fit an existing category. Do not immediately edit implementation; capture the evidence and perform root-cause classification first.

productionShadowProtocol.taxonomyIsFrozen: Do NOT invent new categories after observing results merely to make SHADOW appear successful. If a genuinely new category is required, document why the frozen taxonomy was insufficient - the taxonomy being wrong is itself a result.
productionShadowProtocol.taxonomyRelationshipToEngineTaxonomy: This is the OPERATIONAL layer above the 15-category engine taxonomy in shadow-comparison.ts. They are not competing vocabularies: the engine taxonomy classifies a comparison; this taxonomy classifies a finding an operator must act on.

abortGates.rule: SHADOW must be aborted if evidence indicates any of the following.
conditions: customer responses are being modified (any CUSTOMER_MUTATION)
SHADOW can influence the authoritative resolver result
an unreviewed governed artifact can be presented as approved
release identity is not the explicitly intended release
citation identity is being silently broadened or collapsed
production writes occur where observation is required to be read-only
the comparator cannot reliably distinguish legacy from governed representations

telemetry cannot attribute an observation to its correlation, finding and pinned release (deliberately NOT 'cannot identify the resolver path': the v2 event carries no resolver-path identifier at all per KG5D-DISC-01, so that stronger wording would abort every run on its first event; path-level attribution is a known instrumentation limit, not an abort condition)
release/rollback state differs from the expected preflight state
an unexpected condition makes continued observation unsafe or uninterpretable
abortGates.doNotContinueForALargerSample: Do NOT continue collecting data after a hard abort condition merely to obtain a larger sample. A larger sample of uninterpretable observations is not more evidence.

instrumentation proven to measure the customer contract correctly, including a per-observation non-vacuity floor
LEGACY remained the authoritative customer response for the entire observation window
SHADOW was disabled cleanly after the observation window
the evidence is sufficient to make a separate CUTOVER decision

repairs.E1_predicateRole: New predicate-role.ts classifies a matched token as ASSERTED_PREDICATE, NEGATED_PREDICATE, ATTRIBUTIVE_MODIFIER, NP_HEAD or OTHER, by position and morphology. Bounded, hand-rolled, no parser and no dependency -- the same class of analyser as negation-scope.ts and impression-scope.ts.
repairs.E1_contradictionScope: checkContradiction now requires an ASSERTED, UNNEGATED predicate, and draws removal tokens from a strict UNAMBIGUOUS_SERVICE_WITHDRAWAL subset. Bare 'removed' is EXCLUDED because 'the chain guard has been removed' and 'the conveyor was removed from service' are both asserted predicates and only the second withdraws equipment. The negated-hazard test additionally requires the negated phrase's HEAD to be the hazard object (English NPs are head-final, so 'hazard warning labels' denies *labels*, a control) and NO contrastive connector after the scope.
repairs.E1_stateSupportScope: checkStateSupported requires an ASSERTED, unnegated predicate for CORRECTED, CONTROLLED and REMOVED_FROM_SERVICE. NEGATED and HYPOTHETICAL deliberately keep presence semantics -- their markers are particles, not verbs predicated of a subject.
repairs.E1_governingAsymmetry: A vocabulary used to REJECT must be unambiguous; a vocabulary used to ADMIT may be permissive. Section 33.1's lesson one level down, and it is what justifies the different treatment of the two checks.
repairs.E2_prompt: The ladder rule generalised from 'a negation governs only its own clause' to 'EVALUATE EVERY CLAUSE, NOT ONLY THE FIRST -- let the strongest condition claim decide', plus a five-line discriminator: is the thing that could not be observed the fact that DECIDES this candidate? decides it -> INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with a question; decides nothing -> classify from what WAS observed and ask nothing.
repairs.E2_detectorRecordsOnly: observation-availability.ts detects EXPLICITLY_NOT_OBSERVED / OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE / UNSPECIFIED and records them as an ADVISORY issue. It changes NO condition state and removes NO candidate, exactly as the entry contract required. An inability phrase counts only when attached to a PERCEPTION verb, so 'the guard could not be refitted' is not an observation gap; 'failed to' was excluded because equipment fails as readily as inspectors do.

checkScopes.checkContradiction: (A) ACTIVE resting on a negated hazard: fires only when the negated NP HEAD is a hazard object AND no contrastive connector follows the scope. (B) ACTIVE contradicted by a correction or service withdrawal: fires only on an ASSERTED, UNNEGATED predicate drawn from CORRECTION_TOKENS or UNAMBIGUOUS_SERVICE_WITHDRAWAL.
checkScopes.checkStateSupported: CORRECTED / CONTROLLED / REMOVED_FROM_SERVICE require an asserted unnegated predicate; NEGATED / HYPOTHETICAL keep presence semantics.
checkScopes.modifierNegatedNonPredicateHandling: A modifier, a label/name, an object of a preposition and a token under a governing negation may NOT delete or create a finding. Only an asserted predicate may act on the rejection path.
